Babaji, let us walk today with gratitude in our hearts and service in our hands. Where there is doubt, grant us faith; where there is weariness, grant us strength; and where there is need, let us be Your instrument.

Divine One, you are blessed. Babaji, thank You for blessing and supplying all of our needs — finances and faith, health and wealth, peace and love. Our flesh and our heart may fail, but You are the strength of our heart and our portion forever.
Babaji, guide our hands to seva and our hearts to devotion. Let every act of service be an offering, and every offering a step closer to You.
In stillness we find You; in service we express You. Let today's efforts be a quiet prayer of gratitude.
You are the light that does not dim and the strength that does not tire. Walk with us, Babaji, in all that we undertake today.
Let our minds be calm as the mountains and our hearts be open as the sky. Avirat seva mahe — devoted, always, to the seva of humanity.
Every child we reach, every hand we hold, is Your grace working through us. Thank You, Babaji, for the privilege of service.
Babaji, teach us that giving is not what we have left over, but what we choose to offer first.
Let today's seva be simple, sincere and without expectation — service offered for its own sake is service offered to You.
Where we cannot see the way forward, let us trust the One who has already walked it.
Babaji, may our patience outlast our problems, and may our faith outlast our doubts.
A single toy in a child's hands, a single lesson on a screen, a single meal shared — let us remember that no seva is too small to matter.
Grant us the humility to serve quietly, and the joy to serve without tiring.
Babaji, let our work today be worthy of the trust placed in us by those we serve.
In every tribal village, every classroom, every camp — let Your presence be felt through our hands.
May we carry the mountains' stillness within us, even on the busiest of days.
Babaji, remind us that seva is not a duty we complete, but a devotion we live.
Let compassion lead before convenience, and let service lead before self.
Today, let us be a little kinder than is required, and a little more patient than is comfortable.
Babaji, You have asked only that we serve — let that be enough for us today.
May every rupee given and every hour offered return to the giver a hundredfold in peace.
We are not the source of this seva, only its instruments — let us hold that truth with humility.
Babaji, let today's small act of service be tomorrow's lasting change in someone's life.
Where there is division, let us build a toy library; where there is despair, let us bring light.
May our hands stay busy in service and our hearts stay still in devotion.
Babaji, thank You for the privilege of being needed, and the grace of being able to answer.
Let us not wait for the perfect moment to serve — the need before us today is the moment.
In the quiet of the Himalayas or the noise of a crowded classroom, You are equally present, Babaji.
May the seeds of seva we plant today grow into shade for someone we may never meet.
Avirat seva mahe — let this not be a phrase we recite, but a life we live, one day at a time.
